record.title: halo battery door, FDM prototype variant — a 1.200 mm printed wall on the same outer dome, the same three bayonet tabs, matched to the FDM shell's opened clearances
record.why: built from the same parametric source with fdm=True.
record.origin_why: modelled parametrically in ce-cad from Apple's own published dimensional callouts (transcribed in research/fetched/G-apple-airtag-dimensional-drawing.md) and the CC BY 4.0 DXF ordinate table (research/fetched/G-airtag-profile-from-dxf.md); every halo-specific dimension is lane M's own engineering, argued in docs/MECHANICAL.md. Nothing physical has been built or measured. Admitted to the shelf through the TRIAD.md 'generated' door: evidence/ledger.jsonl + a computed trust.json.
record.process: FDM, 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.12 mm layer, no brim
record.frame: origin on the axis at the lowest point of the battery door's outer face (Apple's drawing datum); +z toward the crown apex at z=7.980; +x through the 6 o'clock bayonet ledge. Every halo part is BUILT in this frame, so its placement in the assembly is the identity.
record.source_of_dimensions: design.py at the repo root — the ONE parametric source; cad/part.py imports it
record.note: A printed door cannot be stamped stainless and will not seal to IP67. It exists to exercise the bayonet by hand. NOT queued to any printer.
